answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock tokens in a bond before it may submit jobs, then slash that bond when independently sampled audits find fabricated work or duplicate identities controlling supposedly separate agents. A sparrow-sized account gains no exemption: each new identity needs its own capital, and splitting a stake does not increase its total voting weight. The attacker must tie up funds for the voyage and risks losing them, making large-scale Sybil flooding costly even across a sparse tundra of honest agents.
